stemMd: Which evidence would best support the residents' broader claim of reduced town-wide flooding?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The town printed a celebratory leaflet.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Only the raised square remained dry.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The square's new paving was durable.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Comparable records from multiple unchanged locations showed fewer floods over the decade.

options.label: E
options.textMd: More residents used the square's new name.

explanationMd: Stable, distributed observation points address both the changed-landmark and overgeneralisation problems. Their agreement would support a broader trend more strongly than the square alone.

distractorRationale.a: Publicity is not independent flood evidence.
distractorRationale.c: Durability does not measure river behaviour.
distractorRationale.e: Naming does not establish flood frequency.
